findings.title: apply_model silently ignores the documented 'args' key of dict model specs
findings.description: The apply_model docstring documents the canonical dict spec as {'model': <str or instance>, 'args': [...], 'kwargs': {...}} (both 'args' and 'kwargs' optional), but _resolve_model (core/model.py, params = dict(resolved.get('kwargs', {}))) reads only 'kwargs' and drops 'args' with no error or warning, so the model is silently constructed with default parameters. hyp.apply_model(d, {'model': 'PCA', 'args': [3]}) on (80,8) data returns shape (80,8) instead of (80,3). A spec like {'model': 'KMeans', 'args': [5]} would silently cluster with the default 8 clusters instead of 5 -- silently wrong analysis configuration. Pipeline honors the identical spec (Pipeline([{'model': 'PCA', 'args': [3]}]).fit_transform -> (90,3)), so the two chaining mechanisms disagree on the same documented grammar.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
d = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(1).standard_normal((80, 8)), axis=0)
print(np.asarray(hyp.apply_model(d, {'model': 'PCA', 'args': [3]})).shape)  # (80, 8), expected (80, 3)
from hypertools import Pipeline
print(np.asarray(Pipeline([{'model': 'PCA', 'args': [3]}]).fit_transform(d)).shape)  # (90->80, 3): Pipeline honors args
findings.expected: (80, 3) -- positional args passed to the model constructor as documented, or at minimum a loud error that 'args' is unsupported here
findings.actual: OK: (80, 8)  [t03 case 3: '!!! ARGS SILENTLY IGNORED: got shape (80, 8), expected (80, 3)']; Pipeline form: OK: (90, 3)

findings.title: Dispatcher-built Pipelines (multi-stage return_model, plot bundle['pipeline']) cannot be pickled or hyp.save'd
findings.description: Pipelines assembled by build_pipeline wrap each stage in _DispatchStep whose _call is a lambda defined inside _make_stage_step (core/pipeline.py), so pickle fails with "Can't get local object '_make_stage_step.<locals>.<lambda>'". This breaks the fit-once/save/reuse-later workflow for exactly the objects the docs promote for reuse: the fitted Pipeline returned by any multi-stage return_model=True call (e.g. hyp.reduce(train, reduce='PCA', ndims=3, normalize='across', return_model=True)) and hyp.plot's return_model bundle['pipeline'] (and therefore saving the whole bundle). hyp.save uses plain pickle, so it fails identically. User-constructed hyp.Pipeline objects and apply_model list-pipeline returns pickle and reload correctly with exact transform reproduction, so only the _DispatchStep path is affected. Fix direction: make _make_stage_step return module-level callables/partials or give _DispatchStep __reduce__/__getstate__ support.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pickle, hypertools as hyp
train = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(4).standard_normal((100, 8)), axis=0)
red, bp = hyp.reduce(train, reduce='PCA', ndims=3, normalize='across', return_model=True)
pickle.dumps(bp)  # AttributeError
# equivalently: hyp.save(bp, '/tmp/bp.pkl')
# and: bundle = hyp.plot([train], normalize='across', reduce='PCA', ndims=3, show=False, return_model=True); pickle.dumps(bundle['pipeline'])
findings.expected: Fitted Pipeline round-trips through pickle/hyp.save and reproduces .transform exactly (as the user-constructed Pipeline does: verified match=True)
findings.actual: AttributeError: Can't get local object '_make_stage_step.<locals>.<lambda>' (raised for pickle.dumps(bp), hyp.save(bp, ...), and pickle.dumps(bundle['pipeline']))

findings.title: apply_model(list-of-stages, stack=False, return_model=True) returns a broken Pipeline whose transform crashes
findings.description: In apply_model's pipeline branch, each stage's fitted model under stack=False is a LIST of per-dataset fitted models; the branch appends those lists into `fitted` and constructs Pipeline(fitted), producing steps that are raw Python lists (repr: Pipeline([list=[PCA(n_components=4), PCA(n_components=4)], list-1=[...]])). The docstring promises return_model gives "a fitted hypertools.Pipeline ... so it can be reused on held-out data via .transform()", but .transform() reaches _step_transform's last-resort fit_predict fallback and raises AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'fit_predict'. Pipeline construction also silently accepts the list steps (see finding 010 on constructor validation).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
d1 = np.cumsum(rng.standard_normal((70, 6)), axis=0); d2 = np.cumsum(rng.standard_normal((50, 6)), axis=0)
res, pipe = hyp.apply_model([d1, d2], [{'model': 'PCA', 'kwargs': {'n_components': 4}}, {'model': 'PCA', 'kwargs': {'n_components': 2}}], stack=False, return_model=True)
print(repr(pipe))
pipe.transform(np.asarray(d1, float))  # AttributeError
findings.expected: Either a usable per-dataset model structure (e.g. list of Pipelines, one per dataset) or a clear error that stack=False + list + return_model is unsupported
findings.actual: Pipeline([list=[PCA(n_components=4), PCA(n_components=4)], list-1=[PCA(n_components=2), PCA(n_components=2)]]); pipe.transform(d1): RAISED AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'fit_predict'

findings.title: mode= applies to EVERY stage of a list pipeline, so reduce->cluster pipelines cannot produce labels; mode/method mismatches raise raw AttributeErrors
findings.description: apply_model passes mode unchanged into every stage of a list pipeline, so the natural request hyp.apply_model(data, ['PCA', 'KMeans'], mode='fit_predict') crashes while fitting the FIRST stage with AttributeError: 'PCA' object has no attribute 'predict' -- there is no way to get final-stage cluster labels from a mixed pipeline in one apply_model call (auto mode yields KMeans distance space instead; labels require hyp.cluster with reduce= or two separate calls). Relatedly, any single-model mode/method mismatch surfaces as a bare AttributeError rather than a hypertools error naming the problem and fix: mode='predict_proba' with PCA -> "'PCA' object has no attribute 'predict_proba'"; mode='fit_transform' with DBSCAN -> "'DBSCAN' object has no attribute 'transform'" (from model.fit(...) then model.transform(...) in _apply_single). Docstring does not state that mode is per-stage for list specs.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
d1 = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal((100, 10)), axis=0)
hyp.apply_model([d1, d1], ['PCA', 'KMeans'], mode='fit_predict')  # AttributeError on PCA
# also: hyp.apply_model(d1, 'PCA', mode='predict_proba'); hyp.apply_model(d1, 'DBSCAN', mode='fit_transform')
findings.expected: Either mode applies to the final stage only (stages before it auto), or a clear ValueError like "stage 'PCA' does not support mode='fit_predict'; ..."
findings.actual: RAISED AttributeError: 'PCA' object has no attribute 'predict' | AttributeError: 'PCA' object has no attribute 'predict_proba' | AttributeError: 'DBSCAN' object has no attribute 'transform'

findings.title: supported_models() referenced by the apply_model docstring is not exported from the top-level hypertools namespace
findings.description: apply_model's docstring says string specs are "a registered model name (see `supported_models()`)", and core/__init__.py exports supported_models, but hypertools/__init__.py imports only apply_model and Pipeline. The natural call hyp.supported_models() raises AttributeError; users must know to use hypertools.core.supported_models(). Both my t03 and t10 scripts tripped over this on first write.
findings.expected: hyp.supported_models() returns the 31 registered names (as the docstring implies), or the docstring gives the importable path
findings.actual: AttributeError: module 'hypertools' has no attribute 'supported_models'  (hypertools.core.supported_models() works: 31 names)

findings.title: apply_model and Pipeline resolve string names against different registries (31 vs 41 names)
findings.description: apply_model's registry is REDUCERS+CLUSTERERS+UMAP (31 names); Pipeline._resolve_step_class additionally includes MANIPULATORS and ALIGNERS (41 names: +ZScore, Smooth, Resample, Normalize, HyperAlign, Procrustes, NullAlign, SharedResponseModel variants). So hyp.apply_model(d, 'ZScore') fails with "unknown model 'ZScore'" while hyp.Pipeline(['ZScore']) works, and supported_models() understates what string specs the library accepts in Pipeline contexts. Confusing for users moving between the two documented chaining mechanisms.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
d = np.random.standard_normal((30, 4))
hyp.apply_model(d, 'ZScore')  # ValueError: unknown model 'ZScore'
hyp.Pipeline(['ZScore']).fit_transform(d)  # works
findings.expected: One shared registry (or documented rationale for the difference in both docstrings)
findings.actual: apply_model: ValueError: unknown model 'ZScore'; supported names: [31 names]. Pipeline(['ZScore']).fit_transform(d): OK (80, 8). Pipeline error lists 41 names.

findings.title: Bare class specs rejected by apply_model, and dict-with-class rejected everywhere, with the unhelpful message "unknown model: <class ...>"
findings.description: hyp.apply_model(d, PCA) (bare sklearn class) raises ValueError: unknown model: <class 'sklearn.decomposition._pca.PCA'> from unpack_model -- the message neither says classes are unsupported nor that an instance or registry string would work (the unknown-STRING message does include that hint). The same error hits dict specs with a class inside ({'model': PCA, 'kwargs': {...}}) in BOTH apply_model and Pipeline, even though the Pipeline docstring says a spec is "anything unpack_model accepts: a registry name (string), a class, an already-constructed ... instance, a dict spec ..." -- and Pipeline does accept a BARE class (Pipeline([PCA]) works). So the documented grammar is inconsistent: bare class OK in Pipeline, not in apply_model; class-inside-dict broken in both.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
d = np.random.standard_normal((30, 4))
hyp.apply_model(d, PCA)  # ValueError: unknown model: <class ...>
hyp.apply_model(d, {'model': PCA, 'kwargs': {'n_components': 3}})  # same
hyp.Pipeline([{'model': PCA, 'kwargs': {'n_components': 3}}])  # same
hyp.Pipeline([PCA]).fit_transform(d)  # works
findings.expected: Classes accepted uniformly (instantiated with args/kwargs), or a message like "pass an instance (e.g. PCA()) or a registered name"
findings.actual: RAISED ValueError: unknown model: <class 'sklearn.decomposition._pca.PCA'> (all three failing forms); Pipeline([PCA]) OK: (90, 6)

findings.title: Pipeline.transform promises "without refitting" but silently REFITS steps that lack transform/predict (DBSCAN, OPTICS, ...)
findings.description: Pipeline.transform's docstring: "Apply the already-fitted steps (in order) to `data` without refitting them." For steps with no transform and no predict, _step_transform falls back to np.asarray(model.fit_predict(data)) -- a fresh fit on the new data. Verified: Pipeline(['DBSCAN']) fit on 120-row train, then .transform(50-row test) returns 50 fresh labels computed by refitting DBSCAN on test. Inherent to density clusterers (no out-of-sample predict), but the silent contradiction of the documented contract can mislead scientists into believing test labels come from the train fit. Should warn or document the fallback in Pipeline.transform's docstring (it is only documented on the private _step_transform helper).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np
from hypertools import Pipeline
train = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(3).standard_normal((120, 8)), axis=0)
test = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(4).standard_normal((50, 8)), axis=0)
p = Pipeline(['DBSCAN']); p.fit_transform(train)
print(p.transform(test).shape)  # (50,) -- labels from a NEW DBSCAN fit on test
findings.expected: Documented behavior: either raise (cannot transform without refit) or warn that fit_predict re-runs on the new data
findings.actual: DBSCAN fit_transform -> (120,) ; transform(test) -> (50,) with no warning (silent refit via fit_predict)

findings.title: Fitted pipelines containing TSNE (the flagship gallery pipeline) cannot honor the documented .transform() reuse; raw AttributeError
findings.description: apply_model's return_model docstring promises the returned Pipeline "can be reused on held-out data via .transform()", and the gallery example's showcase pipeline is [PCA, TSNE]. But sklearn TSNE has no transform/predict/fit_predict, so _step_transform's chain of fallbacks exhausts and raises bare AttributeError: 'TSNE' object has no attribute 'fit_predict'. The promise is unqualified and the error does not explain that TSNE cannot embed held-out data. (Same applies to other no-transform manifold models, e.g. SpectralEmbedding/MDS.)
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
d1 = np.cumsum(rng.standard_normal((100, 10)), axis=0)
res, p = hyp.apply_model(d1, [{'model': 'PCA', 'kwargs': {'n_components': 5}}, {'model': 'TSNE', 'kwargs': {'n_components': 2}}], return_model=True)
p.transform(np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(1).standard_normal((30, 10)), axis=0))
findings.expected: A clear error ("TSNE cannot transform held-out data; refit or use a parametric reducer") and a docstring caveat on return_model
findings.actual: RAISED AttributeError: 'TSNE' object has no attribute 'fit_predict'

findings.title: Pipeline constructor silently accepts unusable steps (non-list steps arg, wrong-arity tuples), failing later with cryptic errors
findings.description: Pipeline('PCA') iterates the STRING character by character, raising ValueError: unknown pipeline step 'P' -- technically an error, but baffling. Pipeline([('a', 'PCA', 'extra')]) constructs successfully (the 3-tuple is stored as a step named 'tuple'), then fit_transform raises AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'fit'. Same late-failure pattern lets apply_model's stack=False bug (finding 003) build Pipelines of raw lists. Constructor should validate that steps is a non-string sequence and each resolved step is fit/transform-capable.
findings.repro:
from hypertools import Pipeline
import numpy as np
Pipeline('PCA')  # ValueError: unknown pipeline step 'P'
p = Pipeline([('a', 'PCA', 'extra')])  # constructs
p.fit_transform(np.random.standard_normal((20, 4)))  # AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'fit'
findings.expected: Constructor-time TypeError naming the bad step and the accepted forms ((name, spec) tuple or bare spec)
findings.actual: ValueError: unknown pipeline step 'P'; supported names: ... | Pipeline([tuple=('a', 'PCA', 'extra')]) then RAISED AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'fit'

findings.title: stack=True fits the caller's model instance in place while stack=False clones it; stack=False return_model returns a list even for single input (undocumented)
findings.description: Passing an sklearn instance with stack=True fits THAT object (caller's instance gains components_ etc.); with stack=False each dataset gets a _clone and the caller's instance stays unfitted -- an asymmetric side effect on the caller's object. Additionally with stack=False, return_model yields a LIST of fitted models (one per dataset) even for a single input dataset (['PCA']), while the docstring only describes "the fitted model instance when `model` is a single spec" (true only for stack=True). Both behaviors are reasonable individually but undocumented and mutually inconsistent.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
d1 = np.random.standard_normal((70, 6)); d2 = np.random.standard_normal((50, 6))
inst = PCA(n_components=2); hyp.apply_model([d1, d2], inst, stack=True); print(hasattr(inst, 'components_'))  # True
inst2 = PCA(n_components=2); hyp.apply_model([d1, d2], inst2, stack=False); print(hasattr(inst2, 'components_'))  # False
res, fitted = hyp.apply_model(d1, 'PCA', ndims=2, stack=False, return_model=True); print(type(fitted))  # list ['PCA']
findings.expected: Consistent instance handling (clone in both paths, or document mutation) and docstring coverage of the stack=False return shape
findings.actual: stack=True passed instance now fitted: True; stack=False original fitted: False; single-input stack=False fitted type: <class 'list'> ['PCA']

findings.title: User-constructed Pipeline crashes cryptically on hypertools' canonical multi-dataset (list) input; bare aligner steps reject lists of ndarrays
findings.description: hyp.Pipeline does no stack/unstack (unlike apply_model), so feeding the library's canonical list-of-datasets input to a Pipeline with raw sklearn steps dies inside numpy: Pipeline(['ZScore', PCA-spec, KMeans-spec]).fit_transform([x, y]) raises "ValueError: setting an array element with a sequence... inhomogeneous shape" (ZScore passes the list through; PCA chokes on it). Bare aligner steps are worse: 'HyperAlign' is advertised in Pipeline's supported-names error message, but Pipeline(['HyperAlign']).fit_transform on a list of numpy arrays raises datawrangler's "Exception: Unsupported datatype: <class 'list'>" (from dw.unstack in Aligner.fit); the same call works when the list elements are DataFrames. Nothing documents that user-built Pipelines take a single array (or aligners: DataFrames), and no hypertools-level error explains it. Note the mandatory-focus manip->reduce->align->cluster chain IS fully supported via the dispatcher kwargs/build_pipeline route (verified in t01/t06); only direct Pipeline construction has this gap.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from hypertools import Pipeline
x = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(2).standard_normal((90, 6)), axis=0); y = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(3).standard_normal((40, 6)), axis=0)
Pipeline(['ZScore', {'model': 'PCA', 'kwargs': {'n_components': 3}}]).fit_transform([x, y])  # numpy inhomogeneous-shape ValueError
Pipeline(['HyperAlign']).fit_transform([x[:40], y])  # Exception: Unsupported datatype: <class 'list'>
Pipeline(['HyperAlign']).fit_transform([pd.DataFrame(x[:40]), pd.DataFrame(y)])  # works
findings.expected: Either list inputs stacked/threaded per-step like apply_model, or an early hypertools error stating Pipeline steps operate on a single dataset (and aligners need DataFrames)
findings.actual: ValueError: setting an array element with a sequence. The requested array has an inhomogeneous shape after 1 dimensions. The detected shape was (2,) + inhomogeneous part. | Exception: Unsupported datatype: <class 'list'> | list of DataFrames: OK [(40, 6), (40, 6)]

findings.title: Same model spec yields different result KINDS in apply_model vs Pipeline (GMM: probabilities vs labels; KMeans auto: distances, never labels)
findings.description: apply_model's auto mode prefers predict_proba, so GaussianMixture(n_components=3) returns (n,3) membership probabilities; Pipeline._step_fit_transform prefers fit_transform then fit_predict, so the identical GaussianMixture instance in a Pipeline returns (n,) hard labels. Meanwhile KMeans via apply_model auto returns the (n,k) distance-space fit_transform, so scientists expecting labels from a clusterer get distances unless they know to pass mode='fit_predict' (t10: KMeans OK shape=(60,8) with default k=8). Each behavior matches its own code path, but hyp.reduce/hyp.cluster resolve these models through Reducer/Clusterer wrappers with consistent GH#174 semantics -- apply_model and raw Pipeline bypass those wrappers and disagree with each other.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
from sklearn.mixture import GaussianMixture
from hypertools import Pipeline
d1 = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(42).standard_normal((100, 10)), axis=0)
print(np.asarray(hyp.apply_model(d1, GaussianMixture(n_components=3, random_state=0))).shape)  # (100, 3)
print(np.asarray(Pipeline([GaussianMixture(n_components=3, random_state=0)]).fit_transform(d1)).shape)  # (100,)
findings.expected: The two chaining mechanisms produce the same result type for the same spec (or docstrings cross-reference the difference)
findings.actual: apply_model GMM -> (100, 3) (predict_proba); Pipeline GMM -> (100,) | same? False; t10: KMeans OK shape=(60, 8) [distances, not labels]

findings.title: Gallery example plot_apply_model.py teaches the deprecated {'model','params'} dict form (emits DeprecationWarnings when run)
findings.description: docs/auto_examples/plot_apply_model.py lines 32-33 use {'model': 'PCA', 'params': {'n_components': 5}} / {'model': 'TSNE', 'params': {'n_components': 2}} -- the LEGACY form that unpack_model deprecates. Running the example verbatim emits two DeprecationWarnings telling users not to write what the example just taught them. The example should use the canonical 'kwargs' form (which would also sidestep finding 001's args ambiguity).
findings.expected: The flagship apply_model example uses the canonical {'model': ..., 'kwargs': {...}} form with no warnings
findings.actual: DeprecationWarnings from gallery-example spec form: 2 ["{'model': ..., 'params': {...}} is deprecated; use {'model': ..., 'args': [...], 'kwargs': {...}} instead"]

findings.title: plot_pipelines_return_model.py example aligns 200-row train with 80-row test, triggering the trim warning and discarding 60% of the training data
findings.description: The multi-stage demo hyp.reduce([train, test], reduce='PCA', ndims=3, normalize='across', align='HyperAlign', return_model=True) uses train (200 rows) and test (80 rows); HyperAlign trims to the common 80 rows, emitting "UserWarning: alignment keeps only the 80 row(s) common to all datasets; datasets with more rows were trimmed." (twice per run, also from the hyp.plot bundle cell). A tutorial teaching the recommended reuse pattern should not itself demonstrate silently-lossy usage; equal-length datasets (or a note about the trimming) would fix it.
findings.repro: MPLBACKEND=Agg python docs/auto_examples/plot_pipelines_return_model.py  # observe UserWarning from hypertools/align/common.py:47
findings.expected: Example data chosen so the align stage does not trim rows (or explicit discussion of the trim behavior)
findings.actual: UserWarning: alignment keeps only the 80 row(s) common to all datasets; datasets with more rows were trimmed. Align datasets with matching numbers of observations to avoid dropping data. (emitted twice per run)
